comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the digest prompt is unbounded — a long session overflows the digest model's window**

`generateHandoffDigest` defaults `tokenBudget: 0`, which in `prepareBranchEntries` means *no limit*: the whole branch's serialized conversation rides ONE summarizer prompt (`generateBranchSummary` → `<conversation>` block), and `streamFunctionSumarizer` sends it as a single user message (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:819`).

The compaction pipeline bounds exactly this with `summarizationPayloadBudget(summarizerWindow)` + chunk/fold (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:544`, issue #729) so a summarizer never receives a payload past its own window. The handoff path bypasses that machinery: on a long session (the primary handoff use case) the digest call overflows the digest model's window (typically the smol role) → provider 400/413 → `handoff digest failed: Summarization failed: …` — on precisely the sessions where a handoff is most wanted. Some providers truncate oversized input silently instead of erroring, which would produce a quietly partial digest instead.

Suggested fix: resolve the slot's context window (`slot.model` is available at the call site in `agent_cli_handoff.dart`) and pass a bounded `tokenBudget`, or route the digest through the same payload-budget/chunk-fold guard the compaction digest uses. Note this finding and the resident-window truncation (comment 1) are two sides of the same input-bounding gap: windowed input is silently truncated, full-open input is unbounded.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Ctrl-C cannot cancel the digest call — the issue #1085 M3 interrupt contract is not honored**

Compaction wires its summarizer to the user's interrupt: `_runAutoCompact` creates a `CancelTokenSource`, bridges `_agent.cancelToken` into it, and stores it in `_activeCompactionAbort` so Ctrl-C during "Compacting context…" stops the LM call (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart:819-823`; `_abortRunOrCompaction` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart:35`).

`_handoffSlash` passes **no** `cancelToken` to `generateHandoffDigest` — the parameter exists on the API but is dead in the CLI wiring. During the "Writing handoff digest…" phase, Ctrl-C runs `_abortRunOrCompaction()`, which (with no `_activeCompactionAbort` set) only latches the sticky `_runAbortRequested = true` and aborts nothing: the digest LM call grinds to completion — potentially minutes for a big digest (see comment 2's unbounded payload) — and the sticky abort flag even rides into the FRESH session until the next prompt resets it.

Suggested fix: mirror the compaction wiring — create a `CancelTokenSource` around the `generateHandoffDigest` call, register it (or bridge the agent token into it), pass `token` into `generateHandoffDigest(cancelToken:)`, and clear it in the `finally`. The `digest.aborted` → "handoff interrupted" path is already implemented and tested; it just can never fire today.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the editor invocation is POSIX-quote-only — the edit step silently never works on Windows**

`handoffEditorCommand` wraps the digest path in POSIX single quotes (`'…'` with `'\''` escaping). Production `exec` on Windows runs the command via `cmd /c` (`LocalShell._childCommand`, `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`), where single quotes are **literal characters**: the editor receives `'C:\…\.fah\handoff-digest-<ts>.md'` — quotes included — as the file name.

Consequences on a supported platform (gh-2115 just repaired Windows REPL behavior, so Windows is in scope):
- The editor cannot open the real digest file; the flow degrades with a misleading note (`editor exited (exit N) — using the digest as generated`) that invites the user to debug their editor when our quoting is the cause.
- Worse, some editors open a *new* buffer for the nonexistent quoted name — the user edits and saves that buffer, and the handoff proceeds with the **unedited** digest with no visible anomaly at all.

Suggested fix: platform-aware quoting for the editor argv (double quotes + `"`/`^` escaping on Windows), or bypass the shell for this call with an argv-split exec seam so `FA_EDITOR="code --wait"` still works. A Windows-specific test (or a documented POSIX-only caveat on the feature) would pin whichever behavior lands.

# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `/handoff` on a resumed session digests only the resident window

**Fixed in `7b82ef8e6a`** (`lib/src/compaction/handoff_digest.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_handoff.dart`), fix direction 1 with the loud degrade you asked for.

- `collectEntriesForHandoff` now primes **whole-ledger residency before the branch walk** — `session.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (the established read-everything escape hatch, `session_tree.dart:325`, the same one the trajectory `view`/`cost`/`inspect` verbs use). The resident-tail truncation can no longer happen: the whole branch is resident when `getBranch` runs.
- The `tooLarge` backstop refusal (`WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder`'s gh-1073 pre-check) **propagates** out of `collectEntriesForHandoff` — it is never swallowed. `_handoffSlash` catches `SessionException(code: tooLarge)` and degrades LOUDLY: a plain (non-dim) line — `handoff: the session ledger exceeds the whole-ledger residency bound — the digest will cover only the resident tail; the old session keeps the full history` — plus the exception's own repair-hint message, then continues over the resident branch via the new `collectResidentBranchForHandoff` fallback. The digest is never presented as complete when it is partial.

**Regression test — windowed open (the resume path), as requested** (`test/compaction/handoff_digest_test.dart`):

- `a windowed (resumed) session collects the WHOLE branch, not just the resident tail…` — builds an 800-record session, reopens `windowed: true`, walks with the parity budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident(tokenBudget: 50)`), asserts the windowed branch IS partial (the bug precondition, verified RED: collect returned **50 of 800** records before the fix), then asserts `collectEntriesForHandoff` returns all 800.
- `a ledger past the whole-ledger bound refuses with the tooLarge SessionException…` — pins the propagate-don't-swallow contract (`maxWholeLedgerBytes: 1`).

Full-storage sessions (the existing suite's `repo.create` shape) are a no-op for the priming — behavior unchanged there.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread 2 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the digest prompt is unbounded

**Fixed in `7b82ef8e6a`** (`lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart`, `lib/src/compaction/handoff_digest.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_handoff.dart`) — routed through the same payload-budget/chunk-fold guard the compaction digest uses (your suggested fix option 2), which also resolves the "two sides of the same input-bounding gap" asymmetry without sacrificing the whole-branch digest contract.

- `generateBranchSummary` gains `int? maxPromptTokens` (default `null` = byte-identical legacy path, pinned by a new no-op-parity test). Over budget, it summarizes **chunk-wise**: `chunkSummarizableMessages` splits the region (chunk plan sized with the same 4096-token envelope reserve the compaction fold uses), each chunk's conversation is bounded by `truncateForSummaryBudget` (a single oversized message gets the explicit `[… N more characters truncated]` note, never silent), and every later call folds the prior summary in as `<previous-checkpoint>` — the result is the LAST fold. Abort/failure on any chunk surface as `aborted`/`error` on the result; the never-throw contract is kept.
- `generateHandoffDigest` gains `int? summarizerWindow` + `CompactionSettings settings` and computes `summarizationPayloadBudget(summarizerWindow, settings)` — the exact bound the #729 compaction payloads ride.
- The CLI call site passes `slot.model.contextWindow` (the digest model's own window — typically the smol/memory role) and `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, mirroring how `AutoCompactorFactory` passes `(sources.smolModel ?? sources.mainModel).contextWindow`.

**Tests** (`test/compaction/handoff_digest_test.dart`):
- an over-budget branch (~21k tokens vs a 32k-window smol role's 16384-token budget) is summarized chunk-wise: >1 call, **every outbound prompt ≤ budget** (the IT-C1 invariant), later prompts carry `<previous-checkpoint>` + the prior fold, and the composed digest still carries the handoff preamble + the `<read-files>` list (file ops accumulate across ALL entries even when the conversation rides chunks);
- an under-budget branch with a window set produces **byte-identical** prompt to the unbounded path (single call);
- a single message bigger than the budget is truncated with the explicit note.

# Thread 3 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Ctrl-C cannot cancel the digest call

**Fixed in `7b82ef8e6a`** (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_handoff.dart`) — exactly the wiring you suggested, mirroring `_runAutoCompact`'s #1085 M3 pattern:

- `_handoffSlash` now creates a `CancelTokenSource` around the `generateHandoffDigest` call, registers it in **`_activeCompactionAbort`** — the slot `_abortRunOrCompaction()` and all three interrupt routings (line REPL, TUI `onInterrupt`, headless) already consult — passes `abort.token` into `generateHandoffDigest(cancelToken:)`, and clears the slot in the `finally`.
- The run-token bridge is in place too (`_agent.cancelToken.onCancel → abort.cancel`), matching the compaction wiring, so a mid-run invocation cancels with the run.
- Note the routing shape: `/handoff` runs outside a run bracket (`isBusy` false), so Ctrl-C hits the `else if (_activeCompactionAbort != null)` arm — the digest call is cancelled ALONE, no sticky `_runAbortRequested` latch, no `_agent.abort()`, and the "handoff interrupted" receipt (already implemented and tested, previously unreachable) finally fires.

**Test** (`test/cli/agent_cli_handoff_test.dart`, verified RED before the fix — `timed out waiting: interrupt note`): `Ctrl-C cancels the digest call (#1085 M3)…` — the digest call hangs on the cancel token (`AbortableStreamFunction`), `io.interrupt()` fires, "handoff interrupted" prints, no editor ran, no session switch, and the next prompt completes a fresh run normally (`followup.calls ≥ 1 && !cli.isBusy`) — proving the sticky abort flag never rode out of the cancelled digest call.

# Thread 4 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the editor invocation is POSIX-quote-only

**Fixed in `7b82ef8e6a`** (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_handoff.dart`, `lib/src/cli/host_shell_stub.dart` / `host_shell_io.dart` + the conditional import in `agent_cli.dart`) — platform-aware quoting (your suggested fix option 1):

- `handoffEditorCommand(editor, path, {bool? isWindows})` now quotes for the HOST shell the env's `exec` actually runs the command under:
  - POSIX `sh -c`: the unchanged single-quote form (`'…'` with `'\''` escaping) — byte-identical to before, so every existing editor-sim test and the `EditorSimEnv` command-shape pin still hold;
  - Windows `cmd /c` (`LocalShell._childCommand`): **double quotes** with defensive `"` doubling — no single quote ever reaches the argv, so the editor receives the real digest path instead of a quoted (nonexistent) file name. Inside double quotes cmd treats `^` literally, so no caret escaping is needed.
- The Windows arm is reachable in production via the new `hostShellIsWindows` probe (`Platform.isWindows` behind the web-safe conditional-import pattern this library uses for every `dart:io` seam — see `process_probe_stub.dart`/`process_probe_io.dart`).
- Both arms are **unit-pinned** (`test/cli/agent_cli_handoff_test.dart`, `handoffEditorCommand platform quoting`): the POSIX test asserts the single-quote shape incl. the `'\'` escape for an embedded quote; the Windows test asserts `code --wait "C:\work\.fah\handoff-digest-1.md"` and that the command contains no single quote at all. The `isWindows` pin exists because the CI runners cannot exercise `cmd /c` in situ.

No POSIX-only caveat needed: the edit step now works on both platforms.

comments.body:
**Summary**: The `/handoff` core is well built (branch-digest reuse, lossless old session, thorough tests, green suites), but the digest input is unbounded in both directions: on a resumed (windowed) session it silently digests only the resident tail (verified: 3 of 40 records), and on a full-open long session the digest prompt overflows the summarizer's window — so the feature fails or lies precisely on the long sessions it exists for. Two smaller gaps: Ctrl-C cannot cancel the digest call, and the Windows editor invocation can never open the digest file.

**Key Issues**:
1. 🚨 `handoff_digest.dart:75` — windowed sessions digest only the resident window, silently (BLOCKING, reproduced)
2. ⚠️ `handoff_digest.dart:87` — `tokenBudget: 0` sends the whole branch as one unbounded summarizer prompt
3. ⚠️ `agent_cli_handoff.dart:50` — no `cancelToken` wired; Ctrl-C cannot stop the digest call
4. ⚠️ `agent_cli_handoff.dart:19` — POSIX-quote-only editor command is broken under Windows `cmd /c`

**Next Steps**:
1. Make `collectEntriesForHandoff` read the whole branch on windowed sessions (`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` precedent) or print a visible truncation note when `hasOlder` remains; add a windowed-open regression test
2. Bound the digest payload via `summarizationPayloadBudget(summarizerWindow)` / chunk-fold as compaction does
3. Wire `_agent.cancelToken` → `CancelTokenSource` → `generateHandoffDigest(cancelToken:)` so `digest.aborted` becomes reachable
4. Quote the editor argv per-platform (double quotes on Windows) or exec it without a shell

**Digest (ranked, non-thread)**:
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_handoff.dart:174` — `_switchToHandoffSession` skips `_usage.reset()`/`_meter.reset()` + `_flushUsageLedger()` (which `_switchToMetadata` performs on every switch): the fresh session's `/stats` and footer open with the old session's tok/cost/turn (mirrors `/reset`, which shares the gap)
- `lib/src/compaction/handoff_digest.dart:97-101` — the conversation-less guard walks `prepareBranchEntries` (whole-branch token estimation) a second time before `generateBranchSummary` repeats it internally
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_handoff.dart:19` — third private re-implementation of POSIX single-quote quoting (`shellQuote` in `lib/src/cube/backends/cube_backend.dart:54`, `q()` in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart:462`); consolidate when the Windows quoting fix lands

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: `/handoff` on a resumed session digests only the resident window — the truncation is silent**

`collectEntriesForHandoff` reads the branch through `session.getBranch(...)`, which on a windowed storage returns only the *resident* records:

- Every resumed/booted CLI session is opened windowed — `_loadSessionInner` does `_repo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:868`).
- `WindowedSessionStorage.getPathToRoot` "stops silently at the window edge" (`lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart:48`).
- The resume walk `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident(tokenBudget:)` stops as soon as the projected branch tokens cover the parity budget (`lib/src/session/session_tree.dart:285`, issue #503) — for a marathon without a compaction boundary that leaves only the tail resident.

Reproduced on this branch (temporary probe, since removed): a 40-record session, reopened windowed and walked with the resume budget → `collectEntriesForHandoff` returns **3 of 40 records**, `hasOlder` still `true`, no note printed. The digest is then generated from the tail alone, and the fresh session is seeded with it as a complete checkpoint — while this file's own docstring promises "the whole conversation is what a handoff carries over" and the PR description says "whole current branch".

This is the feature's primary flow: resume a long session → work more → `/handoff`.

Fix direction (pick one):
1. Bring the branch fully resident before collecting — `session.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` is the established read-everything escape hatch (`lib/src/session/session_tree.dart:307`, used by the trajectory surfaces); catch its `tooLarge` backstop refusal and degrade loudly.
2. At minimum, print a visible truncation note when the storage still has older pages after the walk (`getStorage() case WindowedSessionStorage(hasOlder: true)`), so the user knows the digest is partial and the old session must be consulted.

Please also add a regression test that opens a session windowed (the resume path), not just via `repo.create` (full storage) — the current suite cannot see this class of bug.
